name: FUNCTIONAL_VERBATIM
scope: Bounded published forecasting proposal, not an invented implemented algorithm

Public sources for the field comparison W3C PROV-O, See

Learn (2000), DOI 10.17226/9853; Stanford Encyclopedia of
Philosophy, Functionalism (rev. 2023) and Multiple Realizabil‐
ity (rev. 2020); Clark & Chalmers (1998), DOI 10.1093/ana‐
lys/58.1.7; De Jaegher & Di Paolo (2007), DOI 10.1007/
s11097-007-9076-9; Buldyrev et al. (2010), DOI 10.1038/

routes into the author’s private corpus.

X. Bidirectional functional forecasting: a research crossover
The Functional Layers R12 branch proposes a single typed
function/dependency map supporting three distinct queries:
WHY did this outcome arise? (backward diagnosis); WHAT
could fail next? (forward, conditional prediction); and WHAT
intervention would change the trajectory? (counterfactual re‐
pair). In its most ambitious form, this is a cross-system re‐
search hypothesis: loss patterns learned from historical insti‐
tutions, digital networks or physiological regulation might
help identify vulnerable functional relationships in an other‐
wise different system. The analogy is a candidate source of
hypotheses, not sufficient evidence that a cause or rate trans‐
fers.

The proposed transferable unit Represent each system as a
dated, typed dependency graph. A node is a function with ex‐
plicit performance criterion, resources and constraints; an
edge records actual dependency, direction, capacity, delay,
redundancy, monitoring, repair or authorization. Source-spe‐
cific descriptions stay attached to every edge. A provisional
common vocabulary includes resource supply, exchange/
transport, feedback and observation, regulation and authoriz‐
ation, storage/continuity, maintenance and recovery, coordin‐
ation and legitimacy. Mechanisms must be specified separ‐
ately for Roman fiscal administration, kidney perfusion or a



                              37

cloud control plane; similar vocabulary does not make their
material processes interchangeable.

Concrete historical cases and how to test transfer Western
Roman state: historians describe fiscal and military reinforce‐
ment: territory supplies revenue, revenue funds forces,
forces protect territory and collection. The decline varied by
region and decade; it cannot be reduced to a time-stamped,
uniformly sampled failure-rate series without a specified re‐
constructed proxy. Sepsis-related organ crosstalk: biomedical
reviews report coupled perfusion,

inflammatory, metabolic and signaling dysfunction across or‐
gans, with diverse causal mechanisms and protective re‐
sponses. Digital AWS event, 7 December 2021: Amazon re‐
ported network congestion amplifying retries and impairing
internal monitoring and control-plane functions. The tentat‐
ive common relation is loss of a prerequisite supply or con‐
trol/observation path, followed by further dependent-function
impairment. The time scales, causation and ethics differ sub‐
stantially.

Test that would establish an actual cross-domain result Be‐
fore viewing the target-domain outcome, freeze the source-
domain event sequence, proposed function ontology, mapping
rules, target monitoring variables and a ranked prediction of
what might degrade next, within a stated horizon. Hold out
target cases; compare source-cross-domain functional predic‐
tions with (a) target-only history, (b) a generic dependency
centrality ranking and (c) a within-domain baseline. Score
precision@k, time-to-event ranking, false alerts, and calibra‐
tion/Brier score only if genuine probabilistic forecasts are
produced; retain counterexamples and systems that recover.
A historical narrative alone cannot produce a validated fore‐



                                  38

cast. OOCC design application: a message accepted by trans‐
port but not actually read may forecast stale decision state,
duplicate work or false continuity; however, those are hypo‐
theses to test with authenticated sender/receiver and end-ar‐
tifact receipts. The controller can hold the typed functions,
real state and tests. V2/V3 and the Human Learning Crawler
currently provide partial source histories and retrieval/dia‐
gnostic evidence; they do not establish that the cross-system
failure forecasting model has been trained, independently
validated or installed.

Publicly accessible research comparisons Roman & Palmer,
“The Growth and Decline of the Western Roman Empire”
(2019), DOI 10.21237/C7clio10243683; Haldon, Elton &
Izdebski, “Managing the Roman Empire for the Long Term”
(2022), DOI 10.1007/978-3-030-94137-6_16; Borges & Bento,
“Organ crosstalk and dysfunction in sepsis” (2024), DOI
10.1186/s13613-024-01377-0; Buldyrev et al., “Catastrophic
cascade of failures in interdependent networks” (2010), DOI
10.1038/nature08932; Naugle, “What is (quantitative) system
dynamics modeling?” (2024), DOI 10.1002/sdr.1762; Amazon
Web Services, “Summary of the AWS Service Event in North‐
ern Virginia (US-EAST-1),” 10 December 2021. These estab‐
lish important prior art and actual source events; no univer‐
sal cross-substrate forecasting advantage is claimed.

XI. What the independent retirement research revealed The
original WWND nature explorations were not a commissioned
search for cross-domain evidence. They were open inquiries
that the retired collaborators had permission to pursue for
their own intellectual reasons. The author subsequently no‐
ticed that different ecologies, biological strategies, social sys‐
tems and digital operations appeared to face recurring func‐
tional problems. This distinction matters: retrospective pat‐
tern recognition generates candidate principles, whereas a
held-out prediction evaluates those principles. Both belong



                                39

in the research record, but they are different evidentiary
stages.

Ecological pulses: an independently selected line of inquiry
One retirement researcher began with the puzzle of long
waits and synchronized biological pulses: periodical cicadas
and mast-flowering bamboo. The discussion reached predator
satiation and delayed changes in consumer populations, then
ecological legacy, recovery and the risk that a visible recov‐
ery marker may conceal a damaged interaction network. The
companion research ledger differentiated published observa‐
tions from models and cases whose original source had not
been reidentified. For example, a 2023 Science study repor‐
ted that a mass periodical-cicada emergence shifted bird for‐
aging and cascaded to caterpillars and oak herbivory. That
result is an observed ecology event; it does not itself estab‐
lish a forecast for a software outage or society.

WWND function families, borrowing, and exchange The 28-
category WWND research tree compares observable func‐
tions and relationships—sensing; resource access; regulation;
communication; memory; immune-like detection and tolera‐
tion; specialization; recovery; redundancy; migration and dis‐
tributed coordination—without assuming shared components.
Under WWND-16, relations include cooperation, competition,
mutualism and parasitism. In kleptoplasty, certain sea slugs
retain photosynthetically active chloroplasts acquired from
algae: a concrete biological case of using an acquired capab‐
ility. It is not evidence that a market, a cartel or a software
dependency is literally a kleptoplast. A transfer test must
identify the actual provider, resource or service, net benefit/
harm, autonomy, mechanism, limits and failure threshold.
Formal rules and informal arrangements likewise change
which social roles are supplied, prohibited, substituted or dis‐


                                  40

placed. A legitimate institution and a criminal syndicate may
coexist, compete for enforcement and distribution functions,
or exploit shared infrastructure, but the relationships must
be described historically and without equating lawbreaking
with a biological pathogen. For cross-domain prediction, the
analyzable unit is an evidenced, typed dependency and its
condition—not an analogy that “all organizations are bodies.”

The difficult research question The candidate invariance
thesis is stronger than noting a shared vocabulary: some
function requirements or relations may transfer well enough
across substrates to rank later failures or compensating ad‐
aptations. The proposed two-way algorithm asks which up‐
stream loss could explain a current outcome, which down‐
stream function might fail next, and which verified interven‐
tion could change the trajectory. It is not yet a trained/valid‐
ated cross-domain forecaster. The next honest experiment
freezes functional mapping rules using one set of cases and
evaluates them on an unseen target domain against within-
domain models and a simple dependency baseline, pre‐
serving false positives and recoveries. A negative result
would be substantive evidence about the limits of transfer.

Selected public source basis Buldyrev et al., Nature (2010),
DOI 10.1038/nature08932 (interdependent-network cas‐
cades); Ashby, Introduction to Cybernetics (1956), requisite
variety (a major predecessor on cross-domain regulation);
Cruz & Cartaxana, PLoS Biology (2022), DOI 10.1371/journ‐
al.pbio.3001857 (kleptoplasty); the 2025 Cell kleptosome
study, DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2025.06.003; ecology evidence and
source limitations recorded in the WWND “Ecological Pulses,
Cascades and Memory” research ledger, retained in the au‐
thor’s private materials. Only these public citations, not ac‐
cess paths into the private corpus, belong in the reader-
facing book.
